thread:
alex_k: Heads up — nightly evals on the v4 model show a big jump in hallucination failures for the ConversationalQA prompt set. Failing rate 2.1% -> 9.8% since last night. Anyone able to triage?

maria_g: I glanced at a few examples, it's mostly long-context prompts where the output truncates and then goes off the rails. Short prompts look ok.

sam_r: Two likely suspects: tokenizer changes in v4 (new merges + small vocab reshuffle) and KV-cache alignment. If token ids shift, cached key/value indexing could return stale context.

alex_k: Note we shipped a tokenizer config change: `add_prefix_space=true` plus a couple of merge alterations. That can change tokenization for leading spaces which affects indices. Logs from canary attached in the eval artifacts.

eva_c: Reproduced locally — example: prompt id 5842 gold: "In 1998, ..." v3 -> full paragraph; v4 -> "In 19" then hallucinated unrelated content. Token boundaries show an extra token break at the comma.

qa_bot: NightlyAlert: model=v4 dataset=conversationalqa metric=hallucination_rate delta=+7.7% link=https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly/17925

sam_r: Quick experiment: run the same eval with KV cache disabled (simulate fresh attention every token). If failure rate drops down, that's strong evidence the cache is key.

alex_k: Try this quick repro: `export KV_CACHE=false && python tools/run_eval.py --model=v4 --promptset=conversationalqa --output=/tmp/v4-no-kv.json`

maria_g: Ran that just now — with KV disabled failure rate falls to 2.4%. So KV + tokenizer mismatch is the primary failure mode.

sam_r: Good confirmation. Root cause is: cached KV keyed by token index + tokenizer produced different tokenization than previous version used to populate KV. When we serve mixed versions or upgrade tokenizer without invalidating cache, keys don't line up.

eva_c: Could also be exacerbated by int8 quant paths: small numeric differences in layernorm/softmax can amplify misaligned attention. But KV mismatch explains the abrupt truncation.

alex_k: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) rollback v4 on the hosted canary, 2) hotfix to invalidate KV on model/tokenizer checksum change, 3) add on-load compatibility check that refuses to serve if tokenizer mapping incompatible, 4) add unit/regression test in the nightly harness.

maria_g: I'll open the issue with failing snippets and add a failing-sample bundle for QA to keep. Assigning to @sam_r for the hotfix.

sam_r: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 — Patch adds tokenizer checksum to model metadata and invalidates session KV on mismatch. Also adding a flag `FORCE_KV_RESET=true` for rollouts. ETA EOD.

deploy_bot: Rollout action: rollback start model=v4 scope=canary nodes=2 started_at=2026-03-20T14:12:08Z

alex_k: Sam — please add an e2e test that loads a v3 tokenizer, encodes a prompt, then loads v4 with different merges and ensures KV is reset (simulate both streaming and non-streaming paths). Also include quantized int8 path.

sam_r: Will add tests: `tests/test_kv_tokenizer_compat.py` with permutations (v3->v4, different add_prefix_space). Will also add a CI job to run against quant kernels.

eva_c: After the rollback on canary the nightly alert rate went back to baseline. We should still prioritize the PR + docs update so future brings don't slip.

qa_bot: NightlyAlert: cleared for model=v4 on conversatio nalqa after canary rollback.

alex_k: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: sam to merge hotfix, maria to update onboarding checklist (tokenizer checksum & kv invalidation), ops to coordinate a safe re-deploy once PR lands.

maria_g: I'll update docs and add a checklist item: "verify tokenizer checksum matches previous version OR force KV reset on rollout".

sam_r: PR opened, tests in progress. Will ping here when green.

eva_c: Adding the small set of failing prompts to the regression suite now so we catch this in future nightly runs.

alex_k: Great. Keeping this thread as the triage record. If anyone finds other regression clusters (e.g., embeddings drifting), post them here so we can correlate. :thumbsup:
